beats.say: Godzilla is a prehistoric monster, but his breath is a warning.
You might expect a giant lizard to just be a movie monster, but he is a prehistoric reptile powered by nuclear radiation.
The original film was an allegory for the effects of the atomic bomb, and the consequences such weapons have on Earth.
His name is a romanisation of Gojira, which alludes to his size, power, and aquatic origin.
Developed by Toho, the monster is an offshoot of radioactivity and ancient creatures, making him indestructible.
His atomic breath is not just a power, it is a representation of the destructive force that created him.
He is a walking history lesson. Which version of the monster is your favourite?

facts: Godzilla is a prehistoric reptilian monster awakened and powered by nuclear radiation.
In the original film, Godzilla was an allegory for the effects of the atomic bomb, and the consequences that such weapons might have on Earth.
The name Godzilla is a romanization of the original Japanese name Gojira.
The word Gojira alludes to the size, power and aquatic origin of Godzilla.
As developed by Toho, the monster is an offshoot of the combination of radioactivity and ancient dinosaur-like creatures, indestructible and possessing special powers.
